name: Antico Molino Caputo "00" Chef's Flour, 1kg
description: Antico Molino has been producing the best flour possible in Naples, Italy since 1924. When making pizza, pasta or bread, the quality of the flour determines the quality of the finished product. Their "OO" flour is their signature product. Named "OO" for the finest setting on the mill, it is high in protein and gluten, resulting in an optimal crust with just enough moisture, crunch, and chew.

name: Antico Molino Caputo "00" Pasta Fresca Flour, 1kg
description: Antico Molino has been producing the best flour possible in Naples, Italy since 1924. When making pizza, pasta or bread, the quality of the flour determines the quality of the finished product. Their Pasta Fresca & Gnocchi flour is designed especially for these two things. It's elasticity & high protien content will produce a superior end result!

name: Antico Molino Caputo Semolina Flour, 1kg
description: Antico Molino has been producing the best flour possible in Naples, Italy since 1924. Finely ground with semolina’s signature yellowish tint, this flour is ideal for traditional pastas and breads. The perfect flour to use when the distinctive color, rustic texture and flavor characteristics of semolina are desired.

name: Caputo Fioreglut Gluten Free Flour, 1000g
description:
The Antimo Caputo line of flours is one of Italy’s premium brands for authentic

Neapolitan pizza, bread, and desserts. Their Fioreglut Gluten Free Flour is a great all-

natural alternative for those allergic to or avoiding gluten. You’ll be pleasantly surprised

at how pizza crust and bread made with this flour achieve a texture and taste that

resembles traditional loaves and crusts.

name: Michele Ferrante No-Soak Controne Beans, 300g
description: Controne beans are an incredibly special bean. This small, round, slightly oval-shaped white bean is an heirloom bean from the Controne Municipality in Salerno (just southeast of Naples). Controne Beans have been listed in the Slow Food Ark of Taste as a bean of cultural importance on the verge of being lost. Controne beans were originally cultivated by Benedictine monks in Salerno. Oh, and most importantly, they taste really good and you don't have to soak them!

name: Strianese Borlotti Beans, 400g
description: Strianese, founded in 1965, is an agricultural coop located in coastal Puglia and Tuscany that specializes in canned tomatoes, vegetables, and legumes. Strianese farmers harvest only at the peak of ripeness. The produce is canned in less than 24 hours using state of the art technology, preserving freshness, color, and flavor. Strianese Fagioli Borlotti is a large variety of kidney bean, plump and pinkish-brown in color with a creamy texture. Excellent in salads and casseroles.

name: Strianese Butter Beans, 400g
description: Strianese, founded in 1965, is an agricultural coop located in coastal Puglia and Tuscany that specializes in canned tomatoes, vegetables, and legumes. Strianese farmers harvest only at the peak of ripeness. Using state of the art technology, the produce is canned in less than 24 hours, preserving freshness, color, and flavor. Their Bianchi di Spagna, also known as butter beans, are large white beans with a tender, creamy texture. They are part of traditional sausage and bean soups and also make an excellent side salad dressed with lemon and tarragon.

name: Strianese Cannellini Beans, 400g
description: Strianese, founded in 1965, is an agricultural coop located in coastal Puglia and Tuscany that specializes in canned tomatoes, vegetables, and legumes. Strianese farmers harvest only at the peak of ripeness. The produce is canned in less than 24 hours using state of the art technology, preserving freshness, color, and flavor. Their Fagioli Cannellini are small, delicately flavored white beans. Sometimes called white kidney beans in the States, these beans are used in classic Tuscan white bean dishes. They also make an excellent topping for crostini, or a base for grilled or roasted meats and fish when simmered with tomato, garlic, and guanciale.

name: Acquerello Rice, 500g
description: Acquerello is the ultimate Carnaroli Superfine rice - it is produced and packed by the Rondolino family on the Tenuta Torrone della Colombara Estate in the heart of Piedmont’s Vercelli province. From aging to refining to enriching, there are 20 steps that each grain of rice must endure to become Acquerello rice. This painstaking process produces a remarkable carnaroli rice that is recognized as one of the world's finest. The result? Perfect risotto every time.

name: Bartolini Farro, 500g
description: In the hills of southern Umbria, The Bartolini family has been growing olives, grains, and legumes since the 1850's. The production of farro, an ancient hulled wheat, dates back to early civilization. When cooked, its dark, plump berries add sweet, full-bodied flavor, chewy texture, and high nutritional value to whatever you are cooking. It makes a fabulous grain salad or hearty risotto. It is also a great substitute for rice when added to brothy soups.

name: Beretta Superfino Arborio Rice, 2lb
description: The most famous of Italian risotto rice varieties, Arborio is named after the town of the same name in the Po Valley in the Piedmont region of northwest Italy. Short grained and full of starch, this rice has great absorption qualities that produce a creamy sauce and a toothsome texture in your risotto. Be sure to pull the rice off the heat just before it reaches al dente, fold in your condiments and enjoy!

name: Beretta Carnaroli Rice, 2lb
description: Carnaroli rice, compared to the more widely available Arborio, is a longer grain with a higher starch content. Prized for it's capacity to absorb huge amounts of liquid without overcooking, the finished rice has an ultra-creamy, yet toothsome texture. Be sure to pull the rice off the heat just before it reaches al dente, fold in your condiments and enjoy!

name: Bluebird Grain Farms Farro, 1lb
description: Bluebird Grain Farms is a family business that was started by Brooke and Sam Lucy in the Methow Valley in 2005. Named for the bluebirds that visit the valley during the growing season, Bluebird's signature grains have set the gold standard for nutrient dense whole grains, fresh milled flour and dry product blends. Their farro has been a staff and customer favorite since the day we first put it on our shelves. It makes a fabulous pilaf, grain salad, or farro risotto. It is also perfect for adding to your sausage and farro soup!

name: Campanini Arborio Rice, 16oz
description: For three generations Campanini has produced custom-milled rice at their small, specialized riseria where each production step is under the supervision of a family member. The rice is pure and natural and does not undergo any chemical treatment. Arborio, the most well known Italian rice, is a very wide and long grain with a central wide pearl. Its high starch content gives the risotto a creamy texture, while staying "al dente."

name: Campanini Carnaroli Rice, 16oz
description: For three generations Campanini has produced custom-milled rice at their small, specialized riseria where each production step is under the supervision of a family member. The rice is pure and natural and does not undergo any chemical treatment. Sought after by chefs for its high starch content, Carnaroli is a long, slender, tapering grain and with a central wide pearl. In addition to being perfect for risotto, it blends well with vegetables and other condiments for rice salad and pilaf.

name: Campanini Vialone Nano, 16oz
description: For three generations Campanini has produced custom-milled rice at their small, specialized riseria where each production step is under the supervision of a family member. The rice is pure and natural and does not undergo any chemical treatment. Vialone Nano is a round, short grain with a central wide pearl. It absorbs twice its weight in liquid and flavor during cooking, making it ideal rice for creamy risotto with vegetables, mushrooms and meats.

name: Casina Rossa Corona Beans, 16oz
description: Imported by our friend's at Ritrovo, these bean are a traditional staple of Abruzzo. Locally known as “the poor man’s meat” for its rich flavor, tender yet meaty texture, and generous size. A natural for pasta e fagioli as well as an excellent substitute for meat.

name: Mahjoub Hand Rolled Couscous, 500g
description: With over 100 years of experience in agriculture, the family owned Les Moulins Mahjoub focuses on producing the highest quality products by using careful harvesting methods and small scale production. In Tunisia, this product is called M'hamsa, which translates into sundried wheat grains. The process starts by hand-mixing semolina, olive oil, water, and salt, and then pressing it by hand through screens. It is then preserved with olive oil and dried in the sun. After drying, the result is a nutty and earthy couscous unlike any other. It is perfect with virtually any Mediterranean or Northern African inspired dish - including stews, braised meats, fish and soups.

name: Matiz Bomba Rice, 1kg
description: It is impossible to make true paella without true paella rice. Grown in the rich soils of the national protected L’Albufera Park of Valencia, this short-grain rice is known for its ability to absorb and hold the abundance of flavors while cooking your favorite rice dishes. It's the essential ingredient for paella and arroz negro - it even doubles as a great risotto rice. Bomba rice absorbs 1/3 more liquid than its traditional counterpart.

name: Matiz Paella Rice, 1kg
description: It is impossible to make true paella without true paella rice. Grown in the rich soils of the national protected L’Albufera Park of Valencia, this short-grain rice is known for its ability to absorb and hold the abundance of flavors while cooking your favorite rice dishes. It's the essential ingredient for paella and arroz negro - it even doubles as a great risotto rice.

name: Moretti Bramata Bianca Polenta, 500g
description: The Moretti family has been growing corn and making polenta since 1922. Known across the world for outstanding quality and standards, Moretti's flour is freshly milled and vacuum packaged to ensure optimum freshness in your pantry. Also known as Friulana, this coarse white polenta is great served warm with butter, and Parmigiano-Reggiano. Top it with a sauteed mushrooms for a main course, or use it as a perfect base grilled fish, chicken, or braised meats.

name: Moretti Bramata Polenta, 500g
description: The Moretti family has been growing corn and making polenta since 1922. Known across world for outstanding quality and standards, Moretti's flour is freshly milled and vacuum packaged to ensure optimum freshness in your pantry. This coarse polenta has a toothsome, hearty texture, making it perfect as a base under braised meats. It is also perfect served with a dollop of creamy mascarpone, or spread on a sheet pan, cut into sections and fried.

name: Moretti Fioretto Polenta, 500g
description: The Moretti family has been growing corn and making polenta since 1922. Known across the world for outstanding quality and standards, Moretti's flour is freshly milled and vacuum packaged to ensure optimum freshness in your pantry. This fine polenta has a smooth, silky texture, making it perfect as a base under braised meats. It is also perfect served with a dollop of creamy mascarpone, or spread on a sheet pan, cut into sections and fried.

name: Moretti Taragna Polenta, 500g
description: The Moretti family has been growing corn and making polenta since 1922. Known across the world for outstanding quality and standards, Moretti's flour is freshly milled and vacuum packaged to ensure optimum freshness in your pantry. Also known as Polenta Nero, this hearty polenta with buckwheat can be used just like it's regular counterpart. It is perfect as a base for braised meats, topped with creamy mascarpone, or spread out on a sheet pan, cut into sections and fried.

name: Principato di Lucedio Arborio Rice, 500g
description: Principato di Lucedio is a rare example of single-estate rice; they grow, harvest, and pack all their own product, skipping the typical consolidation of other growers. This method ensures that each and every grain is handled with the same level of care throughout the entire process, ensuring the best possble quality. Their arborio is a superfino classified rice, named after the nearby commune of Arborio in the province of Vercelli. The rice kernels are shorter than Carnaroli, with a uniform opaque creamy color and a solid white center. Arborio has a high starch content that is released slowly in the cooking process, creating a lush blanket of creamy starch that coats each kernel.

name: Principato di Lucedio Carnaroli Rice, 500g
description: Principato di Lucedio is a rare example of single-estate rice; they grow, harvest, and pack all their own product, skipping the typical consolidation of other growers. This method ensures that each and every grain is handled with the same level of care throughout the entire process, ensuring the best possible quality. Considered the King of Italian rice, Carnaroli is a long oval grain that contains the highest starch content of any risotto rice. The result is an ultra-creamy, velvety risotto, making it the preferred choice for home cooks and chefs alike.

name: Rancho Gordo Alubia Blanca Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. This small, versatile Spanish-style white bean has a creamy texture and holds its shape even with long, slow cooking. Great for soups, salads & bean dips, or any time a recipe calls for Great Northern or Cannellini beans.

name: Rancho Gordo Ayocote Blanco Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. These super-rich, creamy beauties hold their shape through long cooking times. With a potato-like flavor, they are perfect cooked with bacon or pancetta!

name: Rancho Gordo Ayocote Morado Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Ayocote Morado is a "gateway bean." Once you start, you get hooked. It's big, beefy texture is perfect for those trying to cut out meat and eat a more plant-based diet, or for vegetarians who are cooking dinner for their omnivore friends. No one will miss the meat when you toss them with good fruity olive oil, sauteed wild mushrooms, and a little garlic.

name: Rancho Gordo Ayocote Negro Beans, 126oz
description: Produced in Mexico, this thick-skinned bean is big and beautiful. Not your average black bean. It's a firm bean but goes from dense to creamy with continued cooking. Ayocote Negro are firm without being starchy and have a darker, inky bean broth than other runner beans enjoy. They are large, bold and one of the first beans we recommend if you're trying to sell a "steak and potatoes"-type on heirloom beans. Originally from Oaxaca, Mexico, the Ayocote family was one of the first cultivated crops of the Americas. They are grown all over central and northern Mexico. If you plant them, you can enjoy the flowers, eat the pods as a broad bean, or shell them fresh for shelling beans. Please note that this is not a traditional black turtle bean. When cooked, it's very similar to the Ayocote Morado or even Scarlet Runner. For a traditional turtle bean, we suggest our Midnight Black bean.

name: Rancho Gordo Black Quinoa, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo Black Quinoa is a versatile grain! It's quick cooking and works as a replacement for rice, couscous or pasta. Don't forget to add it to soups and stews!

name: Rancho Gordo Buckeye Beans, 16oz
description: A small, dense yet velvety bean that holds its shape and provides a rich bean broth. Easily one of the staff's favorite beans.What a great bean this is! It's quick growing and unique tasting. It goes by a few different names, including Yellow Indian Woman. Buckeye is incredibly creamy, almost more like a classic black turtle bean than anything else. It's dense without being intense, if that makes sense. Buckeye beans can be traced to Montana. Because of the short Montana growing season, these beans have been bred to grow fast and plentiful. You can almost watch the vines grow while standing in the bean fields on a summer day!

name: Rancho Gordo Cassoulet (Tarbais) Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. This bean is West Coast grown from classic French Tarbais seed stock. The most famous bean for a traditional cassoulet but versatile enough to become an everyday favorite. Also great in salads, for baked beans & pasta e fagioli!

name: Rancho Gordo Chiapas Black Beans, 16oz
description: Rare black beans from the Mexican state of Chiapas. Rich and dense without being stodgy, with a unique bean broth. How is it possible to think we need to add another black bean? Well, taste is a huge motivator around here. Our partners at Xoxoc in Mexico sent us some bags of beans they sourced in Chiapas from local farmers. We were first blown away by their appearance: beautiful and shiny, looking almost like glazed pottery. We cooked them and were immediately smitten. The supply is limited so we highly recommend trying them!

name: Rancho Gordo Christmas Lima Beans, 16oz
description: An unusual variation of the classic Lima. It offers a rich, full-bodied flavor, with a velvety chestnut texture. A true revelation for those who think they don't like Limas. Christmas Limas are an intriguing variation on the traditional Lima, thought to have originated in Peru (hence the name Lima). They have a distinct chestnut texture and (according to some) flavor, but it's so subtle that's up for debate. In Italy, you'll find them as Fagioli del Papa or Pope's Beans. Also known stateside as Chestnut Lima and sometimes Calico Beans. Whatever you call them, they've done a great deal to help fix the bad reputation of traditional Lima beans.

name: Rancho Gordo Cranberry Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. These thin skinned Cranberry Beans, otherwise known as Roman or Borlotti, have a soft and velvety texture that makes them one of the most versatile beans in the kitchen. Try them in your next batch of minestrone, pasta e fagioli or New England baked beans.

name: Rancho Gordo Crimson Popping Corn, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans and corn will change any preconceived notion you had of how good these things can taste. All their heirloom varieties are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only brand that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. This traditional popping corn is best made the old-fashioned way, on the stovetop. In a pan, add a little oil to the corn. Top with a lid and heat on medium-low, and keep that pan moving to avoid burnt kernels. Seasoning ideas include but are not limited to salt and butter, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, truffle salt or Spanish smoked pimenton!

name: Rancho Gordo Domingo Rojo Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo Domingo Rojo Beans are a classic red bean, essential to dishes like New Orleans Red Beans & Rice, and equally important to many Caribbean cuisines.

name: Rancho Gordo Flageolet Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo Flageolet beans are a creamy, mild bean, traditionally loved with spring lamb or in cassoulet-type dishes, but we love them best with roasted garlic and tomatoes as a side dish with most anything!

name: Rancho Gordo French Green Lentils, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans & lentils will change any preconceived notion you had of how good these things can look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. These beautiful lentils are a classic French staple. They are small, yes, but they hold their shape remarkably well with long cooking times - remaining intact & densely creamy. Perfect with a piece of salmon & sauteed greens!

name: Rancho Gordo Garbanzo Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. With their slightly nutty flavor, these garbanzos are the creamy-textured backbone of our hummus, the key ingredient in your next great batch of falafel, and the foundation to an amazing bean salad.

name: Rancho Gordo Hominy, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. This is nothing like the hominy you've tried from a can. Serve cold in salads, or add to soups, stews, and classic southwestern Posole. Leftovers can be pureed for hominy grits.

name: Rancho Gordo King City Pink Bean, 16oz
description: An heirloom bean from King City, California, with a rich history and a dreamy bean broth. It has a thin skin and a dense yet creamy interior. You would think these pink beans would be a good substitute for the small, pink Santa Maria Pinquitos, but they're not. King City Pinks are closer to Buckeye; dense but not stodgy, they have a thin skin and produce a rich bean broth. We are in love.

name: Rancho Gordo Marcella Beans, 16oz
description: From heirloom Italian seed, this thin-skinned cannellini is named after Italian cooking hero, Marcella Hazan, who encouraged our growing it. A delicate tribute to a mighty force of nature. Marcella beans are grown in California from Italian Sorana seedstock. Sorana is a cannellini bean with incredibly thin skin and when cooked properly, an indulgent creamy texture. You can use them in your kitchen as you would any small white, European-style bean, but with an ingredient like this, simple is often better.

name: Rancho Gordo Mayocoba Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo Mayocoba Beans are creamy and versatile. The bean has a pale yellow hue and super soft texture. Mild-flavored, it soaks up all the flavors of the cooking pot.

name: Rancho Gordo Midnight Black Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Small and creamy, these versatile black beans are great for everything from chili to salads to simple rice and beans.

name: Rancho Gordo Moro Beans, 16oz
description: Beautiful markings and a dense, rich flavor make this super rare bean a favorite. Almost a marriage between a black bean and a pinto but unique in its own right. Raw, the markings have to be among the prettiest of all our heirloom beans, but it's when they've been cooked that you'll be especially happy with them. with a rich, dense texture and a bean broth that you could eat alone as a soup, without the beans! This bean was first spied in Puebla, Mexico. The design was so beautiful and detailed, it wasn't clear they were even a bean. Later we found farmers in Hidalgo who were growing a version with just a touch of purple mixed in and we were smitten. A local cook told us that at the end of the growing season, the women plant the beans and harvest them as young greens and sauté them in butter. A rarity in Mexico, just like the Moro bean itself.

name: Rancho Gordo Pinto Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Quick cooking, creamy and versatile, these pintos are perfect for pot or refried beans, soups and casseroles.

name: Rancho Gordo Puglia Lentil, 16oz
description: Firm, nutty lentil prized throughout Italy and commonly eaten on New Year's Day for good luck. Grown for Rancho Gordo in Puglia, Italy. So much good food comes from Puglia (pronounced Pool-ya, more or less), and these Lentils, or lenticchie in Italian, are no exception.Lentils are prized in the Mediterranean, and most Italians would agree that the best lentils come from Southern Italy. We're ecstatic to offer you this new crop harvest for a limited time.Use them as you would any lentil but be sure and try them in a salad. Their delicate, nutty flavor is perfect at room temperature.Some of us grew up with lousy food co-op bulk bin brown lentils and might be a little hesitant to try these. We think these are very easy to like.

name: Rancho Gordo Rio Zape Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Rio Zape is the classic heirloom bean that inspired the birth of Rancho Gordo. Suggestions of chocolate and coffee make this pinto-family rarity one of our favorite and most requested beans. Great in soups, dips & casseroles.

name: Rancho Gordo Royal Corona Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Royal Coronas are enormous, thick-skinned runner beans with a surprisingly creamy interior. They are more velvety than Greek and Spanish gigandes, and a little more dense than traditional Italian coronas. They are perfect for soups, pasta e fagioli, casseroles, cassoulet, salads and even dips. Fully cooked, they can be a little starchy - be sure to keep cooking until they reach the creamy point.

name: Rancho Gordo Santa Maria Pinquito Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. These small, dense orbs produce a beefy bean broth. Great with any steak coming off the grill and perfect at home in meatless meals. Also great as a pot bean, in chili & stews.

name: Rancho Gordo Santanero Negro Beans, 16oz
description: Prized black beans from Oaxaca with rich flavor and a renowned bean broth. Smaller than your average black turtle beans, these tiny heirlooms are creamy and rich. The bean broth is so distinct that the beans are also known as Siete Caldos, or Seven Broths.

name: Rancho Gordo Scarlet Runner Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo Scarlet Runner Beans are a big, beefy bean with gorgeous markings. Cooks from starchy to creamy and is a constant chef's favorite!

name: Rancho Gordo Vaquero Beans, 16oz
description: A classic chili bean that holds its shape through long, slow, cooking and exudes a generous, dark, rich broth. A really lovely cousin to the Anasazi bean, Vaquero have intriguing black and white markings, not unlike an appaloosa horse might don. The flavor is somewhat like the Anasazi but it's a little lighter. The real fun is the inky, black pot liquor. It looks cool and tastes great.

name: Rancho Gordo Whipple Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Their Whipple Bean is an heirloom from the Willamette Valley. It is somehow both light and substantial. They look very similar to the classic Cargamanto bean from Colombia and they are likely related to the Spanish Tolosana bean from the Basque region. Perfect for baked beans, soups, dips, casseroles or pot beans.

name: Rancho Gordo Wild Rice, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans and grain will change any preconceived notion you had of how good these things can taste. All their heirloom varieties are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only brand that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Although this wild rice takes a little time to cook (about an hour), the results are well worth it. Cook with minced vegetables in water to develop the chewy texture and rich nutty flavor. Use in casseroles, holiday stuffing or serve as a perfect side dish.

name: Rancho Gordo Yellow Eye Beans, 16oz
description: Rancho Gordo beans will change any preconceived notion you had of how good a bean could look and taste. All the heirloom beans they sell are grown with skill and care. Needless to say, they are the only beans that we use in the kitchen at DeLaurenti. Creamy, rich and mild, these Yellow Eye Beans are the foundation of traditional New England Baked Beans. They can also be used just like navy beans, making them great in casseroles, dips and soups.

name: Ritrovo Selections Two Cheese Polenta, 250g
description: Imported by our Seattle neighbor, Ritrovo Selections, this golden polenta is blended with a mixture of cow and sheep's milk cheese. Simple and quick to prepare, serve with tomato sauce and garnish with a generous amount of Parmigiano-Reggiano.

name: Ritrovo Selections White Polenta w/Truffle, 250g
description: Imported by our Seattle neighbor, Ritrovo Selections, this white corn flour with dried truffles couldn't be easier to prepare. Simple and quick to cook, just top it with sauteed mushrooms and you have a dish that can stand alone or work as a side for poultry or meat.

name: Sclafani Lupini Bean, 16oz
description: Sclafani Brand Lupini Beans are soaked and ready to eat right out of the jar! Great in salad's, pasta, or a part of your antipasti platter!

name: Sclafani Lupini Bean, 8oz
description: Sclafani Brand Lupini Beans are soaked and ready to eat right out of the jar! Great in salad's, pasta, or a part of your antipasti platter!

name: Strianese Chick-Peas, 400g
description: Strianese, founded in 1965, is an agricultural coop located in coastal Puglia and Tuscany that specializes in canned tomatoes, vegetables, and legumes. Strianese farmers harvest only at the peak of ripeness. The produce is canned in less than 24 hours using state of the art technology, preserving freshness, color, and flavor. These firm and nutty ceci beans are perfect for absorbing other flavors and spices, making them a must-have for soups, curries, and even falafels.
